children: JPMorgan said it remains bullish on global foreign exchange carry trades despite the recent market pullback, citing a solid growth outlook. According to Sina Finance, strategist Anthony DeLair and others wrote that global and emerging-market carry portfolios have fallen from their mid-September highs, but the decline appears too large relative to the fundamentals reflected in rate markets.

The report added that JPMorgan still prefers global FX carry trades because economic growth is expected to remain solid. It also said further selling in short-term U.S. rates remains a risk, while Latin America-related exposure has been sharply reduced; among current long positions, the Indian rupee and the Indonesian rupiah together account for 25%.

title: JPMorgan Remains Bullish on Global FX Carry Trades Despite Pullback
